Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $U$ be smooth irreducible affine of dimension $i\ge1$ and let $L$ be a nonzero finite-rank local system. By [F3] choose $i$ functions with finite nonempty common zero set $S$. Local complex orientation and local constancy identify $H_S^{2i}(U,L)$ with $\bigoplus_{s\in S}L_s$, which is nonzero, while [F1] gives $H^{2i}(U,L)=0$. The support long exact sequence therefore gives $H^{2i-1}(U\setminus S,L)\ne0$. Cover $U\setminus S$ by the $i$ principal opens $D(f_j)$. Every finite intersection is affine, so [F1] bounds its ordinary cohomology by $i$; the Čech index is at most $i-1$. In total degree $2i-1$ only the term $H^i(D(f_1\cdots f_i),L)$ can contribute, and nonvanishing of the total group forces it to be nonzero. For $i=0$ the detector is simply the nonzero stalk on an isolated point.

The forward direction of the affine-open characterization is [F1], applied to each restriction. Conversely suppose all positive $H^q(V,K)$ vanish. Write $U_i=Y\setminus F_{i-1}$ and argue downwards in $i$ that the stalk degrees on $U_i$ obey the upper perverse support bound. Suppose the assertion is established on all larger-dimensional layers. On $U_i$ let $A=\tau_{\le-i}K$ and $Q=\tau_{>-i}K$. On higher-dimensional layers the induction hypothesis already gives the upper perverse stalk bound, preserved by ordinary truncation; on $W_i$ truncation makes the degree at most $-i$. These are exactly the upper perverse bounds for $A$ on $U_i$, without any claim that $U_i$ has dimension $i$. Thus on each affine $V\subset U_i$, [F1] and the triangle $A\to K\to Q$ give $H^q(V,Q)=0$ for $q>0$. All ordinary cohomology sheaves of $Q$ are supported on the closed smooth layer $W_i\subset U_i$ and are local systems there.

If $Q$ is nonzero, let $b>-i$ be its largest nonzero cohomological degree and let $L=\mathcal H^b(Q)|_{W_i}$ be nonzero on a connected component. The finitely many smooth irreducible components of $W_i$ are disjoint and closed in $U_i$; remove the components where $L$ is zero and all but one nonzero component, and choose an affine open $V_0\subset U_i$ in the resulting open, meeting the retained component. Then $V_0\cap W_i$ is smooth affine and $L$ is a nonzero local system on it. Step 1.1 supplies a principal open of it with nonzero $H^i(L)$. Since $W_i\cap V_0$ is closed in the affine $V_0$, the defining function lifts from its coordinate-ring quotient to a function on $V_0$; localizing the latter gives an affine $V\subset U_i$ with $H^i(V\cap W_i,L)\ne0$. The closed embedding $e:V\cap W_i\hookrightarrow V$ has exact pushforward, and $Q|_V=e_*e^*Q|_V$ because all its cohomology is supported there. Thus $H^a(V,\mathcal H^t(Q))=H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})$. In the bounded spectral sequence $H^a(V\cap W_i,\mathcal H^t(Q)|_{W_i})\Rightarrow H^{a+t}(V,Q)$, [F1] gives $a\le i$ and maximality of $b$ gives $t\le b$. The nonzero term $(i,b)$ has no incoming differential, since those would start at a larger $t$, and no outgoing differential, since those would end at a larger $a$. It is the sole term in its total degree $i+b>0$, contradicting step 1.2. Hence $Q=0$, completing the descending dimension induction and the converse.

2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle over a
paracompact Hausdorff CW complex, with $n\geq1$. Let $P(E)$, $\gamma_E$,
and $x=e((\gamma_E)_{\mathbb R})$ have the conventions of
[[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]].
For each $b\in B$, choose a complex-linear identification $E_b\cong\mathbb C^n$
and denote the resulting fiber inclusion by
$j_b:\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}\to P(E)$.

With the complex orientation on both tautological lines,
$j_b^*x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})=:x_{\mathrm{taut}}$. For $n\geq2$ this is a
generator of $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^{n-1};\mathbb Z)$, and
$1,j_b^*x,\ldots,(j_b^*x)^{n-1}$ is an integral cohomology basis. Its
coefficient reductions are a basis over every prime field $\mathbb F_p$.
For $n=1$ the fiber is a point, $j_b^*x=0$, and the basis is $1$.
A comparison with a generator given the opposite normalization introduces
one fixed sign; with the tautological Euler normalization above the sign is
$+1$, independently of $b$ and the chosen complex-linear identification.

Assume AC. For a CW pair $(X,A)$ and local system $\mathcal L$, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients:
$$H^n\bigl(C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;\mathcal L)\bigr)\cong H^n(X,A;\mathcal L).$$
For a connected pair, it is the equivariant-Hom complex on cellular chains after the published right chain action is converted to the left action $g\cdot c=c\cdot g^{-1}$; equivalently its cochains satisfy $\varphi(c\cdot g)=g^{-1}\varphi(c)$. The comparison is natural for cellular maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $j:X'\setminus\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ and $u=(f\times1)j$. Over an affine chart of the hyperplane parameter space the complement of the incidence in $\mathbb P^d$ is an affine $d$-space bundle, and $X'\setminus\mathcal X$ is closed in the corresponding bundle over $Y'$; thus $u$ is affine. Apply $R(f\times1)_!$ to the localization triangle $j_!j^*p'^*K[d]\to p'^*K[d]\to i_*i^*p'^*K[d]\to$. By [F1] the first term lies in the perverse lower aisle, so it has no negative perverse cohomology; by proper base change and [F2] the second is $p^*Rf_*K[d]$ and the third is $Rg_*M[1]$. The long exact perverse sequence gives the restriction isomorphisms and the monomorphism. Dualizing the whole construction and using $Di_*=i_!D$, $i^!K'=i^*K'[-2]$ from [F2] gives the Gysin isomorphisms and the epimorphism for $l=1$.

The projective-space cohomology formula gives $Rp_*p^*T=\bigoplus_{a=0}^dT[-2a]$ for every constructible complex $T$, and the identical formula with $d-1$ holds for $p'i:\mathcal X\to X$. To justify the formula as a morphism and not only stalk ranks, cup powers of the tautological Euler class pulled back from $(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ define the map from the direct sum, and on every fibre its map is the usual projective-space cohomology basis, hence an isomorphism by proper base change; the integral power basis is [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]], and tensoring the finite cellular cochain complex with $k$ preserves the basis by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]. For heart objects $A,B$, adjunction therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(p^*A[d],p^*B[d])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$: all terms $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[-2a])$ for $a>0$ vanish by [F3].

Write $F=p^*[d]$. For the product projection $p$, the normal slices to $S\times\mathbb P^d$ are precisely the normal slices to $S$. Thus the stalk and costalk boundary conditions characterizing intermediate extension in [F3] are preserved: on a boundary stratum of dimension $s$ their strict bounds $q<-s$ and $q>-s$ become $q<-(s+d)$ and $q>-(s+d)$ after the shift $[d]$. On the dense open, pullback is the shifted pulled-back local system. The no-boundary characterization in [F3] therefore shows that $F$ takes $\operatorname{IC}_S(L)$ to $\operatorname{IC}_{S\times\mathbb P^d}(p^*L)[d]$. Projective space is simply connected by its even-cell CW structure, so projection induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups and $p^*L$ remains irreducible. Hence $F$ is exact, fully faithful by step 1.2, and preserves simples. Every composition factor of $F(A)$ is therefore a pulled-back simple; for a subobject choose a simple subobject, lift its inclusion by full faithfulness, quotient it out and induct on length. This proves the image of $F$ is closed under subobjects and quotients. The derived right adjoint $Rp_*[-d]$ preserves the lower aisle: for $E\in{}^pD^{\ge0}$ and $B\in{}^pD^{\le-1}$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(B,Rp_*E[-d])=\operatorname{Hom}(F(B),E)=0$. Thus $Rp_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge q}$ into ${}^pD^{\ge q-d}$. Its heart right adjoint is $r={}^pH^{-d}Rp_*$, since the positive-degree truncation of $Rp_*C[-d]$ has no Hom from a heart object. The analogous left adjoint is $\ell={}^pH^dRp_!$, using $p^!=p^*[2d]$. Full faithfulness gives $rF=1$. The kernel of the counit $Fr(C)\to C$ lies in the image of $F$ by subobject closure, and applying the left-exact $r$ shows that kernel is zero, by the adjunction identity $r(\varepsilon_C)=1$. Every subobject $F(B)\hookrightarrow C$ factors through this counit by adjunction. Consequently $Fr(C)$ is exactly the largest subobject coming from $Y$; duality gives the largest quotient $F\ell(C)$.

Put $T=Rf_*K$, $V=R(f\times1)_*p'^*K$ and $U=Rg_*i^*p'^*K$. The graph of $(f,X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d)$ is a closed embedding $a:X\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbb P^d$ and $f=q a$, where $q$ is the projection. Closed pushforward is perverse-exact directly from the two stratum inequalities in [F3]: on strata inside the image its stalks and costalks are those of $K$, and on the complement they vanish. Applying the lower-aisle calculation of step 2.1 to $q$ therefore gives $T=Rq_*a_*K\in{}^pD^{\ge-d}$. Under the cup-power bases of step 1.2, the map $Rp_*V\to Rp_*U$ is a matrix $(1,\beta):\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]\oplus T[-2d]\to\bigoplus_{a=0}^{d-1}T[-2a]$: restriction carries each of the first $d$ parameter-class powers to the identical power on the incidence bundle, while the last power may be a linear combination involving base classes. Changing coordinates by $(x,z)\mapsto(x+\beta z,z)$ identifies this map with projection. Its discarded summand $T[-2d]$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge d}$, so the map induces isomorphisms in every perverse degree below $d$, including degrees $-1$ and $0$ for all $d\ge1$. This uses no decomposition of $T$ into its perverse cohomology.

Set $n=d-1$. Step 1.1 gives an isomorphism $L={}^p\tau_{<n}V\simeq{}^p\tau_{<n}U$ and a monomorphism $\iota:{}^pH^nV\hookrightarrow{}^pH^nU$. Apply $Rp_*$ to the two triangles $L\to V\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to$ and $L\to U\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}U\to$. Their five-term exact sequences are ${}^pH^{-1}Rp_*L\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*V\to{}^pH^{-1}Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}V\to{}^pH^0Rp_*L\to{}^pH^0Rp_*V$ and the same sequence for $U$. The first and fourth vertical maps are identities, and the second and fifth are isomorphisms by step 3.1; the five lemma proves that the middle map is an isomorphism. For either $W=V$ or $W=U$, the triangle $({}^pH^nW)[-n]\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W\to{}^p\tau_{\ge n+1}W\to$ has last term whose $Rp_*$ lies in ${}^pD^{\ge n+1-d}={}^pD^{\ge0}$, by step 2.1. Its perverse cohomology in degrees $-2$ and $-1$ vanishes. The resulting exact sequence gives, naturally in $W$, ${}^pH^{-1}(Rp_*{}^p\tau_{\ge n}W)\simeq{}^pH^{-1-n}(Rp_*{}^pH^nW)=r({}^pH^nW)$, since $-1-n=-d$. Thus $r(\iota)$ is an isomorphism. Proper base change and exact $F$ give ${}^pH^nV=F({}^pH^{-1}T)$, so its right adjoint is ${}^pH^{-1}T$. Adjunction factors $\iota$ as the counit $Fr({}^pH^nU)\to{}^pH^nU$ preceded by the isomorphism $F(r(\iota))$. By step 2.1 its image is exactly the largest pullback subobject of ${}^pH^nU={}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$. Apply this result to $DK$ and dualize using [F2] and [F3]; the middle object is dualized, perverse degrees change sign, and largest subobject becomes largest quotient $F({}^pH^1T)$. This proves every assertion.
